The '''[[1947 in association football|1947]]–[[1948 in association football|48]] season''' was the 49th completed season of [[The Football League]].

==Final league tables==

The tables below are reproduced here in the exact form that they can be found at [https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1947-48.html The Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation] website<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1947-48.html |title=England 1947–48 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=2010-02-24}}</ref> and in ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79'',<ref name=" Rothmans"/> with home and away statistics separated.

Beginning with the season 1894–95, clubs finishing level on points were separated according to goal average (goals scored divided by goals conceded), or more properly put, goal ratio. In case one or more teams had the same goal difference, this system favoured those teams who had scored fewer goals. The goal average system was eventually scrapped beginning with the 1976–77 season.<ref name="Rothmans">Ian Laschke: ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79''. Macdonald and Jane’s, London & Sydney, 1980.</ref>

From the 1922–23 season, the bottom two teams of both Third Division North and Third Division South were required to apply for [[re-election (Football League)|re-election]].<ref name=" Rothmans"/>

[[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], the most successful English club side of the 1930s, picked up their first postwar silverware, finishing top of the First Division by seven points. Their nearest rivals were [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], who lifted the [[FA Cup]] with a dramatic 4–2 win over [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley]] to end their 37-year wait for a major trophy. [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] finished level on points with [[Matt Busby]]'s team. [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]], the 1946 FA Cup-winners, finished fourth in the league. Defending champions [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] finished 11th.

[[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]] were relegated in bottom place, 14 points adrift of safety, and were joined in the Second Division by [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]].
